endorsements.quote: Additionally, algorithms should be developed and validated using data from diverse populations, and investigators should report subgroup-specific metrics of predictive validity.
Special attention should be given to the identification, exploration and proper discussion of societal and data biases before model development.

The implementation of critical checkpoints and continuous monitoring of clinically implemented algorithms will also assist in determining which algorithms are performing fairly, and if not, what changes can be made to improve them.

unlisted_practices: Explicitly include individual-level socioeconomic determinants in the development and validation of cardiovascular risk prediction models.
Ensure AI algorithms are explainable and interpretable to all stakeholders so that potential biases can be identified and addressed.
Explore differential rates of missing data and differential misclassification as sources of bias in algorithms.
Consider lowering risk score thresholds for lower socioeconomic status groups to prioritise vulnerable subgroups for non-invasive preventive intervention.
Apply fairness constraints such as equalised false positive and false negative rates during model development.
Investigate the ethical and legal ramifications of positive discrimination in healthcare before implementing such models.
